headline: Norway Work Visa 2026: Skilled Worker Permit Explained
metaDescription: Norway skilled worker visa 2026: salary floors NOK 545,400 for bachelor's and NOK 624,700 for master's, job offer first, NOK 6,300 fee, permit up to 3 years.

sections.content:
The skilled worker permit is how the overwhelming majority of non-EU professionals get to Norway. Three things must be true: you qualify as skilled, you have a concrete job offer, and the pay is right. The Directorate of Immigration, known as UDI, accepts three kinds of qualification: a completed university or university college degree, a completed vocational training programme of at least three years at upper secondary level with a Norwegian equivalent, or, rarely approved, six or more years of specialist experience.

The job must actually require the qualification you have. A software engineer offered a warehouse job does not qualify. UDI itself warns that the experience route rarely succeeds, so treat it as a last resort. Norway has no points system, no golden visa and no digital nomad visa: the skilled worker permit is the one main front door.
sections.title: Who Counts as a Skilled Worker

sections.content:
Norway has no minimum wage law, but it effectively has one for immigration. For positions requiring a master's degree, pay must be at least NOK 624,700 a year before tax in 2026. For positions requiring a bachelor's degree, it must be at least NOK 545,400 a year. If a collective agreement applies in the industry, you must be paid the collective wage rate instead.

UDI may accept a lower salary if you document that it is normal for the occupation and place, but this takes substantial evidence. Separately, Norway has legal minimum wages in ten sectors, including construction, electricians, fish processing, hospitality and cleaning. The standard full-time week is 37.5 hours and the law gives 25 working days of vacation a year.
sections.title: The 2026 Salary Floors

sections.content:
You need a concrete offer from one specific employer in Norway. The job must normally be full-time, although UDI accepts at least 80%, and you must not work remotely unless that is part of the job you were granted a permit for. Since early 2026, employers must confirm the offer directly to UDI through its digital system before you can even submit your application.

The employer then gives you a code of four English words, which you enter in the application form. This step was added after fraud problems with fake job offers. The application fee is NOK 6,300 for adults, including renewals, and family immigration costs NOK 11,900 for an adult and NOK 5,950 for a child under 18.
sections.title: The Job Offer and the Confirmation Code

sections.content:
A skilled worker permit is granted for up to three years at a time for jobs requiring a degree, and up to one year at a time for jobs requiring upper secondary vocational training. UDI says it takes up to one and a half months before a caseworker even opens a complete application, and clean cases are decided after that, so total processing is typically three to four months.

After three years on a skilled worker permit, you can apply for a permanent residence permit, which costs NOK 4,000 for adults. If you lose your job, you get six months to find another one on the same permit. The early employment start scheme allows some workers to begin before the permit is approved. Always confirm current figures at udi.no before applying, since thresholds are updated regularly.
